input: Draft a short bio for my conference speaker profile

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The bio is about a specific person — knowing their name, title, and professional background is the foundational content needed to write anything at all.
A speaker bio can highlight career history, achievements, research, thought leadership, or personal story — knowing what to include vs. exclude shapes the entire draft.
The conference topic and industry determine which credentials and experiences are most relevant to foreground for that specific audience.
Many conferences impose a strict word or character count; this dictates how much detail can be included and the level of compression needed.
Bios can be written in first person ('I am...') or third person ('Jane is...'), which is a fundamental stylistic choice that changes the entire voice of the piece.
The goal of the bio could be to establish credibility, build a personal brand, drive session attendance, or something else — this determines what to emphasise.
Knowing whether the user has an existing bio to update or is starting from scratch determines how much raw material is already available to work with.

gold.taskTitle: Draft a short conference speaker bio
gold.taskDescription: Write a concise professional biography to appear on a conference speaker profile page.

questions.title: What is your name, current job title, and employer?
questions.description: Capture the speaker's full name, professional title, and organisation to form the factual foundation of the bio.

questions.title: Which specific achievements or expertise should be highlighted?
questions.description: Identify the key credentials, career highlights, publications, or areas of expertise the user wants foregrounded in the bio.

questions.title: What is the conference topic, industry, or audience?
questions.description: Understand the event context so the bio can be tailored to resonate with the specific audience attending.

questions.title: Is there a required word count or character limit?
questions.description: Determine any hard length constraints imposed by the conference organisers to calibrate the level of detail.

questions.title: Should the bio be written in first or third person?
questions.description: Establish the grammatical person and overall tone — formal, conversational, or somewhere in between.

questions.title: What do you most want the audience to think or do after reading it?
questions.description: Clarify the primary goal of the bio — e.g., build credibility, spark curiosity about the talk, or drive follow-on connection.

questions.title: Do you have an existing bio we can adapt or start from scratch?
questions.description: Find out whether there is prior material to work from, which determines how much drafting effort is needed.
